content: ABCA7, or ATP-binding cassette sub-family A member 7, is a protein encoded by the ABCA7 gene in humans. This protein belongs to the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter superfamily, which is responsible for transporting various molecules across both extracellular and intracellular membranes. ABC genes are categorized into seven distinct subfamilies: ABC1, MDR/TAP, CFTR/MRP, ALD (adrenoleukodystrophy), OABP, GCN20, and White. ABCA7 is specifically a member of the ABC1 subfamily, which is unique in that it is exclusively found in multicellular eukaryotes. This full transporter protein is predominantly expressed in myelo-lymphatic tissues, with the highest levels observed in peripheral leukocytes, the thymus, spleen, and bone marrow. Although the precise function of ABCA7 remains unclear, its expression pattern suggests a potential role in lipid homeostasis within immune system cells. Additionally, alternative splicing of the ABCA7 gene results in the production of two transcript variants. From a clinical perspective, protein-disrupting variants in the ABCA7 gene have been associated with an increased predisposition to Alzheimer’s disease. Data from the Icelandic database of Decode Genetics indicates that the presence of inactive variants of the ABCA7 gene doubles the likelihood of developing Alzheimer’s disease.
